findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. It looks like a leftover debugging change and is unrelated to the deadlock fix. All cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, annotations, query history) now run 10x as often. The job timeout is 9 minutes, so runs can overlap with load. It should be reverted.

findings.title: Debug logging at Error level, including full ID lists
findings.body: Each batch logs at Error level, in both the time-based and count-based cleanup and in orphaned-tag cleanup. The log lines include the full slice of IDs, which can be tens of thousands of entries, and they are emitted even when nothing happened or no error occurred. This floods the error logs, inflates log volume and misleads alerting. These look like debug leftovers and should be removed, or reduced to Debug without the ID list.

findings.title: Orphaned tag cleanup condition is fragile and likely mis-scoped
findings.body: fetchIDs builds `SELECT id FROM annotation_tag WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM annotation a WHERE annotation_id = a.id) LIMIT n`. The unqualified `annotation_id` and `id` in the select list depend on name resolution. The subquery is still a correlated read on annotation, so the original MySQL lock interaction may remain. The condition string is also assembled by concatenation, which makes it brittle.

findings.title: SQLite parameter-limit check uses configured batch size rather than actual ID count
findings.body: The check compares the configured batch size to 999 instead of len(ids). Beyond that, the placeholder path is also used for non-SQLite databases with large batches. Postgres allows at most 65535 bind parameters, and MySQL limits placeholders to 65535 in prepared statements. A large configured batch size can therefore make the delete fail. Branching on len(ids) and chunking the deletes would be more robust.

findings.title: Loop termination depends on affected rows, which can cause an endless loop
findings.body: The loop stops only when affected==0. If the IDs fetched in a batch are deleted concurrently by another process, affected is 0 and cleanup stops early even though more rows remain. Stopping when no IDs were fetched would be more accurate.
